source_meta._title: /execute running chat related commands logs "Received chat packet without valid signature" warning

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition client running 1.19 Pre-release 1; new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world with cheats enabled; access to the active client game directory and its logs/latest.log file.
preconditions: Use Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1, which is the first and only affected version listed in the report.
Use an unmodified client without mods, plugins, or datapacks that alter commands, entities, or chat handling.
The selected launcher installation must use a known game directory so that the current session's client log can be found at <game directory>/logs/latest.log.

Create a new throwaway single-player world. Creative mode and a Superflat world are practical choices that keep the creeper visible and prevent it from attacking the player; they are not stated requirements of the report.
Enable cheats so the player can execute /summon and /execute from the in-game chat screen.
Do not execute the trigger command from a command block, a dedicated-server console, or the launcher; the report specifically requires running it from the player's in-game chat screen.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1, then launch that installation. Do not substitute a later pre-release or release.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu version text identifies the running game as Minecraft 1.19 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer and then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The new-world configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Configure the throwaway world for Creative mode, set Allow Cheats to ON, and select the Superflat world type through the world-options screen. Leave the seed unspecified.
steps.success_cue: The world configuration shows Creative mode, commands/cheats enabled, and Superflat terrain selected.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate and enter the world.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned into the new world.

steps.action: Wait before issuing commands until the nearby flat terrain is rendered and normal player movement responds without loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, movement is responsive, and the client is no longer displaying a world-loading screen.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open the player's in-game chat screen.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible and accepts keyboard input.

steps.action: Enter the following deterministic summon command in the chat input. Include the leading slash, but do not press Enter until the complete command is visible.
steps.success_cue: The complete summon command is visible in the chat input field without alterations.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the summon command.
steps.success_cue: The chat screen closes and a creeper appears approximately three blocks from the player on the open terrain.

steps.action: Visually confirm that the summoned entity is a creeper and remains loaded near the player. Do not kill it, leave the area, or exit the world.
steps.success_cue: A living creeper is visible near the Creative-mode player and is available for the @e[type=creeper] selector.

steps.action: Locate the current client's <game directory>/logs/latest.log file. Confirm that it belongs to this running session by checking that its modification time is current, then record its present end position, modification time, or final few lines as a pre-trigger baseline. Leave the game running.
steps.success_cue: The current session's client latest.log has been identified and a baseline has been recorded so newly appended lines can be isolated after the trigger.

steps.action: Return input focus to Minecraft without closing the world, then press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control. Use the player's chat screen rather than any console or command block.
steps.success_cue: The in-game chat input field is open while the creeper remains loaded nearby.

steps.action: Type the report's command exactly as follows, including the leading slash and the capital H in Hi. Do not press Enter until the entire command has been entered.
steps.success_cue: The exact command `/execute as @e[type=creeper] run say Hi` is visible in the chat input field and has not yet been submitted.

steps.action: Press Enter exactly once to submit the command from the in-game chat screen. Do not issue additional commands or repeat the trigger.
steps.success_cue: The chat input closes, the command has been submitted with the creeper selected as its execution entity, and the client log is ready for immediate post-trigger inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The command `/execute as @e[type=creeper] run say Hi` has just been submitted once from the player's in-game chat screen while a loaded creeper exists, and the pre-trigger position of the current client logs/latest.log file is known. Hand off immediately for inspection of newly written client-log entries.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer or a dedicated server. This plan uses the simplest supported topology: a single-player world with an integrated server.

The report does not specify game mode, terrain type, difficulty, seed, or a method for summoning the creeper. Creative mode, cheats, Superflat terrain, and `/summon minecraft:creeper ~ ~ ~3` are practical execution choices intended to create one accessible creeper without introducing combat or exploration.

The operating system and launcher game-directory configuration are not specified. The client log should therefore be resolved relative to the active installation's game directory rather than assuming a platform-specific absolute path.

The report does not require that only one creeper exist. A fresh daylight Superflat world is used to make the deliberately summoned creeper the only likely match, but the trigger command must remain exactly as reported and therefore still targets every loaded creeper.

source_meta._title: Illegal character '\n' in text component clickEvent

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 in a singleplayer world with cheats enabled. The report does not require a dedicated server, multiple players, a particular seed, or a particular game mode.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 release.
Use a singleplayer world in which commands are permitted by enabling Allow Cheats during world creation.

Preserve the report's command exactly. In the embedded run_command value, the text after Players: must contain exactly one backslash followed by the letter n; do not change it to the double-escaped variant.
If controls have been rebound, use the bindings for Open Chat, Submit Command, and primary/left-click instead of the default inputs stated below.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using a launcher installation configured for the exact release version 1.19. Wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left portion of the main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.19, and the menu responds normally.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer and then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Locate the Allow Cheats setting and toggle it until it reads Allow Cheats: ON. Leave the seed, game mode, difficulty, and other world settings at any desired values because the report does not specify them.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen visibly shows Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation and loading to complete. Do not continue while a loading screen is visible.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the singleplayer world, surrounding terrain is rendered, and normal movement and input respond.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat/command input using the Open Chat control; the default key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat interface is open with an editable input field.

steps.action: Paste the report's command into the chat input exactly as supplied. Include the leading slash. Confirm that the embedded text after Players: contains one literal backslash followed by n, not two backslashes.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is present in the chat input, including the leading /tellraw and the embedded Players: followed by exactly one backslash and n.

steps.action: Submit the command by pressing Enter once.
steps.success_cue: The command input closes and a chat component reading Click me! appears in the player's chat output.

steps.action: Open the full chat interface again using the Open Chat control so that its mouse cursor is available. If the Click me! message is not in the currently visible portion of the chat history, scroll until it is visible.
steps.success_cue: The full chat interface is open, the mouse cursor is available, and the Click me! text is visible in the chat history.

steps.action: Move the chat cursor directly over the Click me! text and activate it once with the primary mouse button; by default, left-click. Do not click elsewhere or issue additional input afterward.
steps.success_cue: A single left-click has just been issued on the clickable Click me! chat component, and no subsequent input has been performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just left-clicked the Click me! chat component once while the full chat interface was open. Immediately hand off to the observation subsystem before providing any further player input or dismissing any resulting screen.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, game mode, difficulty, or other world-generation settings; the plan leaves them at arbitrary or default values.
The report does not state whether controls were rebound. The plan uses the default T key for opening chat, Enter for submission, and the primary/left mouse button for activating the chat component.
The command is preserved exactly from the report rather than replaced with either of the alternative commands discussed in its results section.

source_meta._title: Debug messages aren't prefixed with gray color indicators

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6 using an unmodified client. Use a fresh single-player world with commands enabled as the simplest deterministic environment; no dedicated server or additional player is required by the report. Use default chat and keyboard controls unless they have been rebound.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, not the listed fix version 1.19.1 Release Candidate 2 or a newer release.
Create or open a world in which the player has permission to execute commands. For a fresh single-player world, set Allow Cheats to ON during world creation.
Ensure chat is not hidden. If necessary, open Esc -> Options -> Chat Settings and set Chat to Shown.
Ensure command feedback is enabled. This is enabled by default in a fresh world; if it was previously disabled, execute /gamerule sendCommandFeedback true before starting the listed steps.
Use a keyboard capable of sending the F3+B debug-key combination. On keyboards where the function row controls media features, the Fn key may also need to be held.
The player must be fully loaded into the world, with normal movement and keyboard input responding.

steps.action: Start Minecraft using the installation for Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, then open the command-enabled test world.
steps.success_cue: The player is present in the world and the pause or loading screen is no longer displayed.

steps.action: Wait for the world to finish its initial loading before sending any input.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the player can move normally, and keyboard input responds without a loading delay.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat input using the Open Chat control; its default key is T.
steps.success_cue: A chat input field is visible at the bottom of the screen and is ready to accept text.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it as the current player.
steps.success_cue: The chat input closes and a command-feedback message concerning the addition of the test tag appears in the chat area. If an insufficient-permission or unknown-command error appears instead, stop and enable commands before retrying in a fresh world.

steps.action: Use the command-feedback message as the control system message. Inspect the left side of that message and confirm that its gray system-message color indicator is visible before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The command-feedback line remains identifiable in chat and has a gray indicator immediately to its left, establishing the report's control condition.

steps.action: With the game world active and no menu or chat input field open, invoke the debug hitbox function once. Hold F3 and tap B; on keyboards that reserve function keys for media controls, hold Fn as well while sending F3+B. Do not invoke the combination a second time before observation.
steps.success_cue: A debug status message indicating that hitboxes were shown or hidden has just appeared in the chat area, confirming that the debug function executed.

stor.handoff_condition: The F3+B debug function has just executed once, and its resulting debug status message is visible in the chat area. Begin observation of that message and its left-side indicator presentation without pressing F3+B again.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, game mode, world seed, operating system, or customized controls. A fresh command-enabled single-player world with default controls is selected as the minimal deterministic setup.
The report permits any debug function and gives F3+B as its example. This plan uses F3+B exactly to avoid introducing an unreported alternative.

The report does not explicitly state the command-feedback gamerule or chat visibility settings. Their enabled states are necessary for the two comparison messages to be visible and are normally present in a fresh world.
No external version verification was needed because the affected version, exact command, and debug-key combination are all supplied directly by the report.

source_meta._title: Screenshot messages aren't prefixed with gray color indicators

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition graphical client running 1.19.1 Pre-release 6. Use a fresh single-player world in Creative mode with cheats enabled and normal command feedback visible. No dedicated server, additional players, seed, resource pack, or datapack is required by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected Java Edition version listed by the report: 1.19.1 Pre-release 6. Do not use the fix version, 1.19.1 Release Candidate 2.
Use the standard graphical game client because the reproduction requires the Take Screenshot control and an on-screen chat overlay.
Create or load a world in which the player has permission to execute /tag. For a deterministic single-player setup, create a Creative-mode world with Allow Cheats enabled.
Leave command feedback enabled so the /tag command produces the system-message control line required by the report.
Ensure chat is not hidden. The chat overlay must be capable of displaying both command feedback and the screenshot-saved message.
If controls have been rebound, identify the key assigned to the Take Screenshot action. Its default key is F2.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select an installation that runs Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running game as 1.19.1 Pre-release 6.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a fresh world. Set Game Mode to Creative and ensure Allow Cheats is enabled, then select Create New World. A specific world seed is not required.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in the world and can use commands.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until nearby terrain has rendered and player movement and controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding chunks are visible and the client responds normally to movement input.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default, to place the cursor in the chat input field.
steps.success_cue: The chat interface is open and an input field is ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's tag command into in-game chat exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the chat overlay displays feedback confirming that the tag named test was added to the executing player.

steps.action: Use the visible /tag command-feedback line as the control system message. Confirm that its gray color indicator is visible, and do not clear or hide the chat overlay before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The command-feedback system message remains visible with its gray color indicator, providing a nearby visual reference for the next message.

steps.action: Without leaving the world, invoke the Take Screenshot control once. Press F2 if the default key binding is still in use; otherwise press the key currently bound to Take Screenshot.
steps.success_cue: A screenshot is taken and a screenshot-saved message appears in the in-game chat overlay. Do not assess that message's color indicator yet.

stor.handoff_condition: The Take Screenshot control has just been pressed once, and the resulting screenshot-saved message is visible in the chat overlay near the earlier /tag command-feedback control message. Hand off immediately for visual inspection of the screenshot message.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, game mode, or world seed. A fresh Creative-mode single-player world with cheats enabled is selected as the simplest deterministic setup that permits the supplied command without adding unrelated server conditions.
The report names F2 as the default Take Screenshot control but does not require the binding to remain unchanged; the bound Take Screenshot action is authoritative if controls were remapped.
No web verification was needed because the report supplies the affected version, exact command, trigger action, default screenshot key, and required comparison message.

source_meta._title: Chat messages can no longer be reported if the chat is enabled

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1. Use two separate vanilla 26.1 client instances authenticated with two distinct Minecraft accounts and a vanilla Java Edition 26.1 dedicated server configured with online-mode=true. The instructions assume the default keyboard-and-mouse controls and English UI labels. Any game mode and world may be used; no particular seed or coordinates are required.
preconditions: The dedicated server is running Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1, not the listed fix version 26.1.1 Release Candidate 1.
The server's server.properties file contains online-mode=true, and the server has been restarted after that setting was established.
Two distinct authenticated Minecraft accounts are available and can be connected to the server simultaneously. Designate them Account A (message sender) and Account B (reporting client).
Both client instances are running unmodified Java Edition 26.1. Avoid proxies, plugins, or mods that rewrite, delete, or replace signed player chat messages.
Both accounts are permitted to use online multiplayer and player chat through their account privacy settings.
Account B has not blocked Account A. If Account A appears blocked in Social Interactions, unblock it before beginning the reproduction.
Account B's Chat setting must be set to its fully enabled state, shown in the English UI as Chat: Shown. Do not use Commands Only or Hidden.
The test message must be sent as an ordinary player chat message by Account A, not with a command, server console, command block, plugin, or system-message mechanism.

steps.action: Start the vanilla Java Edition 26.1 dedicated server whose server.properties file has online-mode=true. Wait until server startup is complete and the console reports that it is ready to accept connections.
steps.success_cue: The 26.1 server is running in online mode and its console has reached the normal ready state, commonly indicated by a line beginning with "Done".

steps.action: Launch the first Minecraft: Java Edition client using version 26.1 and sign in as Account A, which will send the message.
steps.success_cue: Account A is authenticated and the title screen identifies the running game version as 26.1.

steps.action: Launch a separate Minecraft: Java Edition client instance using version 26.1 and sign in as the distinct Account B, which will perform the reporting-menu actions.
steps.success_cue: Account B is authenticated in a separate 26.1 client instance; it is not using Account A's session.

steps.action: On Account B's client, open Options from the title screen, or press Esc and select Options if already in a world. Open Chat Settings, then activate the Chat setting until its value is Shown. Select Done as needed to save the setting and return.
steps.success_cue: Account B's Chat setting visibly reads Shown rather than Commands Only or Hidden.

steps.action: On Account A's client, open Multiplayer, select or add the prepared online-mode server, and join it. Wait until the world and surrounding chunks have rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Account A is present in the server world and can move normally.

steps.action: On Account B's client, open Multiplayer and join the same server. Wait until the world and surrounding chunks have rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Account B is present in the same server session as Account A and can move normally.

steps.action: Confirm from Account B's client that both accounts are connected. By default, hold Tab to display the online-player list, verify that Account A and Account B are both listed, and then release Tab.
steps.success_cue: The server's player list contains both Account A and Account B at the same time.

steps.action: On Account A's client, press T to open ordinary player chat. Type the exact benign test message below without a leading slash, and press Enter once to send it.
steps.success_cue: Account B receives a normal chat line attributed to Account A. Do not continue until that player-authored message is visible on Account B's client.

steps.action: On Account B's client, press the Social Interactions control, which is P by default. If P has been rebound, use the control currently assigned to Social Interactions instead.
steps.success_cue: The Social Interactions screen is open and Account A appears in its player list.

steps.action: In Account B's Social Interactions screen, locate Account A's entry—the account that sent "test message"—and click its Report Player button. Do not select Account B or another player.
steps.success_cue: The Report Player screen for Account A is open and contains a Chat Messages button.

steps.action: Move Account B's mouse cursor onto the Chat Messages button and leave the cursor resting over the button. Do not click the button and do not change Account B's Chat setting.
steps.success_cue: The cursor is stationary over the Chat Messages button on Account A's Report Player screen, ready for the observation subsystem to inspect the button state and any hover tooltip.

stor.handoff_condition: Account B has just moved the cursor onto the Chat Messages button in Account A's Report Player screen while Account B's Chat setting remains Shown and Account A's ordinary player message is still part of the current server chat context. Begin observation immediately without clicking the button or changing settings.
uncertainties: The report specifies an online-mode server but does not name server software. This plan uses a clean vanilla 26.1 dedicated server as the least confounded implementation of that requirement.

The report does not explicitly identify which account must have chat enabled. This plan applies Chat: Shown to Account B because Account B is the client opening the report interface; setting it to Shown on both clients is acceptable but should not be necessary.
The report does not supply message text. "test message" is chosen as a deterministic benign ordinary chat message; its wording is not asserted to be required.

The exact menu capitalization or layout may differ with language, window size, or accessibility configuration. The required setting is the fully enabled Chat state, contrasted in the report with Commands Only and Hidden.
The default P binding for Social Interactions was externally verified, but a locally rebound control should be used if P no longer opens that screen.
